title: Chocolate Cake or Cupcake with White Icing

content.title: About
content.content: A chocolate cake or cupcake with white icing is a soft biscuit base infused with cocoa chocolate and covered with a sweet white frosting made from powdered sugar, butter and vanilla. Perfect for desserts, celebrations and cozy tea times.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chocolate biscuit is often used as a base for multi‑layer cakes.
White icing gets its name from the lack of cocoa mass, but contains milk chocolate or butter.
These cakes are traditionally decorated with fresh fruit, berries or chocolate shavings.
Chocolate consumption can raise serotonin levels, improving mood.

items.title: Antioxidant source
items.content: Cocoa chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the biscuit and a modest amount of fat in the icing provides a quick and sustained energy boost.

items.title: Calcium content
items.content: Dairy ingredients in the white icing add calcium, beneficial for bones.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The batter contains vitamins B1, B2 and B6, which are involved in metabolism.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates endorphin production, enhancing emotional well‑being.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: The icing contains milk and butter, which may trigger reactions in people with dairy allergies.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Cocoa chocolate contains small amounts of caffeine, which may be undesirable for caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cake or cupcake is a calorie‑dense dessert; moderate consumption is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cake in individual slices, paired with ice cream, berry sauce, or fresh fruit. Cupcakes are convenient as a snack; split them and add buttercream or jam for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 7 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Bring to room temperature before serving.
